Fix: #3064 and #1742 

The basic idea is that arrow timestamps with timezones are converted to UTC (this is unnecessary since arrow timezones are stored as UTC already). The precision is converted to 'us' if necessary. It might throw errors if it's impossible to convert values from lower accuracies.

From my understanding of DuckDB's timezone code, the timezone is set on the ```DBConfig.set_variables['TimeZone']```. Hence it is not currently possible to support per-column timezones. 

But I guess this should already be sufficient in most cases.

issue_context.title: Can't pass an Arrow table with a timestamp with timezone column to duckdb
issue_context.body:
#### What happens?

I tried to run a query on `pyarrow.Table`, but the query could not be executed because the table contained a column of timestamp with timezone (e.g. `timestamp[ms, tz=UTC]`).
When I dropped the column and then ran the query, it worked fine.

#### To Reproduce

I first saw this in Python, but the same error occurs in R as well.
(I don't have a ready-to-use Python environment on my computer right now, so I can only provide an R-only example.)

``` r
library(duckdb)
#> Loading required package: DBI
library(arrow, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

tibble::tibble(
  col1 = lubridate::as_datetime("2018-10-07 19:04:05", tz = "UTC"),
  col2 = 1
) |>
  arrow_table() |>
  to_duckdb()
#> Error: duckdb_prepare_R: Failed to prepare query SELECT *
#> FROM "arrow_001" AS "q01"
#> WHERE (0 = 1)
#> Error: Not implemented Error: Unsupported Internal Arrow Type tsu:UTC
```

<sup>Created on 2022-02-10 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

#### Environment (please complete the following information):

 - OS: Linux
 - DuckDB Version: 0.3.2
 - DuckDB Client: Python/R

#### Before Submitting

- [ ] **Have you tried this on the latest `master` branch?**
* **Python**: `pip install duckdb --upgrade --pre`
* **R**: `install.packages("https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/download/master-builds/duckdb_r_src.tar.gz", repos = NULL)`
* **Other Platforms**: You can find binaries [here](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/tag/master-builds) or compile from source.

- [x] **Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?**
comments: I'm sorry, does it look like it is tracked on #1742?
We did not use to have time zone support but we do now so the Arrow integration is simply lagging a little bit. Should be fixed
Similar to #3080 - we have not been mapping `TIMESTAMPTZ` in the various APIs.

@hannes Pardon my confusion, but does "Should be fixed" mean "this should already be fixed" (i.e., "it is fixed") or "we should fix this in the future"? I am dealing with the same arrow tz issue with the latest duckdb build, so I just wanted to make sure that it is indeed the latter.

@erinov1 This issue is currently open and hasn't been worked on yet. This should be fixed means it will be fixed in the near future (Possibly this or next week). A good indication is when the issue is closed.
For what it's worth, I just experienced this with R 4.1.2 using arrow 7.0.0 and duckdb 0.3.2.

I think we should convert to `TIMESTAMPTZ` (i.e. convert to UTC) as a first pass solution to this problem. All our timestamp infrastructure works best with `TIMESTAMPTZ` right now, so that is the most useful conversion from a functionality perspective. I would also guess that multiple different time zones in one column is an uncommon edge case. 

We can add a flag later on that emits a struct of `(timestamp, tz)` pairs instead.

Did some more experimenting. If I have an arrow table and convert to a data.frame then to_duckdb() does not work. But if I start with a data.frame and convert to arrow, then to_duckdb() works. Will experiment more with register_duckdb() and register_duckdb_arrow(). Though I'm still figuring out when to use that vs to_duckdb().

> We can add a flag later on that emits a struct of `(timestamp, tz)` pairs instead.

I think that should be `(timestamptz, tz)`? Right now we don't have any binning functions that take time zones anyway, just timestamp construction functions (e.g., `make_timestamptz` and `strptime`).

> Did some more experimenting. If I have an arrow table and convert to a data.frame then to_duckdb() does not work. But if I start with a data.frame and convert to arrow, then to_duckdb() works.

In my experience the `to_duckdb()`  in not working when having timezone in an Arrow dataset (`open_dataset()`). Please refer to [ARROW-16318](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/ARROW-16318)
I should have specified that the scenarios I tested involved timestamp columns.

> I should have specified that the scenarios I tested involved timestamp columns.

Sorry, I put it wrong: I was also using timestamps with timezone (in fact only 1 timestamp):
`df1 <- tibble(time = lubridate::now(tzone = "UTC"))`

review_comments:
@hawkfish I would appreciate ur opinion on this as well.

I currently read the Arrow data on UTC, but I ignore whatever timezone mask it has.
I think I should probably set it in the config file, and if there is one already set and differs from the one in Arrow, I should throw an error?
On one hand, I guess that doing this is a bit confusing to the user because that requires them to know this will be stored as UTC and then masked to whatever is set in the config file.
On the other hand, do I want to throw an error?

The TZ setting is ephemeral and will go away when the connection is closed, so I don't think it is horribly important for permanent storage. It is an interesting question as to whether we should set the TZ when reading the file, but what if there are two files with different settings being joined on year or something? I think the safest approach is to stick with the user's existing setting. It would also be nice to obtain the TZ value from the file, but that will probably have to wait for the multi-zone timestamp type. (I still think that should be a `STRUCT` but opinions differ!)
Not required, but maybe fold this into `TimestampTZConversion` by passing in numerators and denominators? That might slow it down though.
